skills.trigger: When determining the laterality and compartment of a mediastinal mass on an axial CT scan.
steps: Identify the patient's right side as the viewer's left side of the image, consistent with standard radiological convention.
Locate the mass relative to the great vessels (ascending aorta, superior vena cava) to confirm it is in the anterior mediastinum.
Distinguish the correct side by verifying the mass is on the viewer's left (patient's right), rejecting options that describe the contralateral side despite similar density features.

skills.trigger: When characterizing the internal composition of a mediastinal mass to differentiate between solid, cystic, or calcified lesions.
steps: Inspect the margin of the mass for hyperdense (bright white) areas indicating calcification, specifically looking for a peripheral rim pattern.
Evaluate the central attenuation; distinguish low-density/heterogeneous centers from homogeneous soft-tissue density.
Select the option describing 'calcification' and heterogeneous/low-density center over options describing 'homogeneous density' when a bright rim and dark center are visible.
